# notranslate

*Directive*

A meta tag value and HTML class that stops Google from offering a translation of a page or of part of it.

Narrative: the topic [Snippets and preview controls](../topics/snippet-controls.md) tells the story; this card lists what links to it.

6 claims mention it: 2 from Google's documentation, 3 shown or said at the event (1 confirmed by Google docs, 1 consistent with Google docs, 1 nothing to verify), 1 the author's analysis. A card is a map: cite the claim ids, with the citation given after each claim.

## Google's documentation

Documented in: [meta tags and attributes that Google supports](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/special-tags), [Helping you break the language barrier](https://developers.google.com/search/blog/2008/10/helping-you-break-language-barrier).

- [`D2-C095`](../sessions/D2-S04-controlling-indexing.md) Docs: Google's Search documentation gives notranslate as a rule for a robots or googlebot meta tag or an X-Robots-Tag header, and says the rule opts a page out of all translation features in Google Search. `[D2-C095, docs, Google Search Central, https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/translated-results]`
- [`D2-C096`](../sessions/D2-S04-controlling-indexing.md) Docs: A 2008 Search Central blog post says a meta tag named google with the value notranslate stops Google Translate from translating any of a page's content. `[D2-C096, docs, Search Central blog (14 October 2008), https://developers.google.com/search/blog/2008/10/helping-you-break-language-barrier]`

## Shown or said at the event

Not in Google's documentation first: present those as said at Search Central Live, never as documented policy.

- [`D2-C093`](../sessions/D2-S04-controlling-indexing.md) Stage, Day 2, confirmed by Google docs: The notranslate robots rule tells Google not to offer a translation of the page in search results. `[D2-C093, stage, John Mueller, Day 2]`
- [`D2-C094`](../sessions/D2-S04-controlling-indexing.md) Stage, Day 2, consistent with Google docs: John Mueller said notranslate can also be set in a meta tag named google, and that in that form it also turns off Chrome's automatic translation of the page. `[D2-C094, stage, John Mueller, Day 2]`
- [`D2-C097`](../sessions/D2-S04-controlling-indexing.md) Stage, Day 2, nothing to verify: John Mueller said he dislikes notranslate because automatic translation is a form of accessibility for visitors who cannot read the page's language. `[D2-C097, stage, John Mueller, Day 2]`

## The author's analysis

- [`D2-C098`](../sessions/D2-S04-controlling-indexing.md) Analysis: International sites should remove notranslate from their templates unless translation must be prevented: the robots or googlebot form switches off Google Search's translation features, and John Mueller said the form named google also blocks Chrome's translation for visitors who do not read the language. `[D2-C098, analysis, Ibrahim Anjro]`

## For developers

- `DEV-IDX-09` **SHOULD** · Documented: Leave notranslate and noimageindex out of templates unless translation or image indexing must be prevented (5 of its claims mention it; its own text names it)
